regime: Rotation Lower after NFP (Trend Stops Flipped Down, Volatility Calm)
summary: Jobs day whip. Everything ran up overnight, then reversed after the 8:30 ET payrolls print. NQ gave back the run to close 29,524, up just 0.07 percent but well off its 29,720 high, and its trend stop flipped down. MES fell 0.45 percent to 7,715 and December gold dropped 0.95 percent to 4,477, both flipping their stops down too. Crude was the one that dipped to 88.73 and recovered, closing 91.24 back above its stop. VIX stayed calm near 14.5, so the fade was orderly and controlled.
psychology: Traders were leaning long into the jobs number after the overnight run to new highs. Then the print hit and the move reversed. The lesson is simple. The market can run right up to a scheduled event and turn on the release, so carrying full size into a top tier number is a gamble. Today also flipped the short term trend stops down on NQ, ES and gold, which is exactly the kind of two way tape that whips trend traders in both directions. When the session swings around an event like this, the edge is doing less. Let price pick a side after the dust settles, then trade along with it.

event.name: August nonfarm payrolls (jobs report)
event.consensus: Not captured this run. Traders came in watching whether the August jobs report would keep the door open for rate cuts or push back on it.
event.actual: Not captured this run. The exact payrolls figure sat behind an exchange data agreement that was not accepted in this unattended run, so the read here is the price reaction. Markets ran to new highs overnight, then faded broadly after the 8:30 ET release. NQ gave back its gains to close 29,524, MES fell 0.45 percent, and December gold fell 0.95 percent, with the equity and gold trend stops flipping down.
event.surprise: Not captured as a number. The cross asset pattern, equities and gold falling together while VIX stayed low, is the kind of move you tend to see on a firmer rates read rather than a growth scare.
event.nqReaction: Up overnight to a 29,720 high, then a sharp two way bar on the 12:30 UTC release, then a fade through the RTH session to close 29,524, back near the day's mean and below a flipped trend stop.
event.crossAsset: Broad. MES minus 0.45 percent and December gold minus 0.95 percent both closed lower with NQ. Crude dipped to 88.73 and recovered to 91.24, the lone market still above its stop. VIX ticked up to 14.53 from 14.32 but stayed low. The 10 year yield was not captured this run.

risk.sizing: Keep size reduced. The jobs number whipped the tape and flipped the trend stops down on NQ, ES and gold, so the short term trend is no longer clearly up. Do not chase the flip in either direction. Crude is the one clean long, above a rising stop, and can be sized normally with a stop under 89.42.
risk.openRisk: For the equities the flipped stops are the line. MNQ back above 29,709 or MES above 7,746 on two hourly closes would turn the short term trend back up. Below, MNQ 29,468 and the 29,000 psych, and MES 7,710 then 7,700, are the downside references. December gold stays soft below the 4,496 stop, and a reclaim there is the first repair sign. Crude stays long above 89.42.
risk.note: Labor Day is Monday Sep 7 and the US market is closed, so liquidity thins into the long weekend and can stay thin on the Tuesday Sep 8 reopen. Carry reduced size through the holiday and let the tape settle after the jobs whip. Prop accounts should mind the holiday schedule and any lingering post news volatility. Not financial advice.

fullReport.title: NY Opening Range / HTA OPEN
fullReport.html: HTA OPEN (NY opening range, the 13:30 to 13:45 UTC window): OR high 29,645.25, OR low 29,553.75, width 91.5 points (0.31 percent). Price broke up out of the range at 13:50 UTC, tagged a 29,692 high, then failed and faded the rest of the session, closing 29,524 back below the 29,542 NYVWAP. NYVWAP here is the session average anchored at the 9:30 ET open, and it is price only this run because volume is unavailable on the continuous contract. So the upside break did not hold and sellers had the day. Signals: a classic upside fake out that reversed into a fade. HOF (short only) got its direction on the reversal, and the back into range read printed as price came back inside the OR. Filters for Friday: no CPI or FOMC, so BIR, HOF, MID and BNC are all eligible, but the jobs number made the open a headline driven whip, so treat opening range plays with extra care around the release.

fullReport.title: Momentum Breakout
fullReport.html: E3v2 Momentum Long keeps its filter off for the equity indices. NQ and ES both closed below their trend stops after the fade, so a fresh momentum long would fight the tape. Crude is the one market still above a rising stop, the profile a momentum long wants, but it spent the day recovering a dip rather than breaking out cleanly. The filter is doing its job here: it keeps you out of index longs while the trend stops are flipped down.

fullReport.title: AVWAP Deviation Band
fullReport.html: AVWAP deviation band (MNQ): AVWAP center 29,537, close 29,524 is right on the mean, about minus 0.5 sigma. Bands: plus 2 sigma 29,585, plus 1 sigma 29,561, minus 1 sigma 29,514, minus 2 sigma 29,490. Sigma is tight near 24 for the regular session even though the overnight spike ran far outside it. Volume is unavailable on the continuous contract, so this is price only. The read: inside the regular session there was no clean 2 or 3 sigma extreme to fade, and the big stretch happened overnight on the news. Deviation band fades work best in balance, and today the real move was the event itself.
